attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family with this project's per-TU flags. Applies to a POINTER LOCAL whose value is a base symbol plus a genuine SCALED INDEX (here `j * PREC_STRIDE`, strength-reduced by the compiler to a byte-offset induction variable), consumed by a memory reference carrying a compile-time constant offset. Says nothing about a pointer local initialised from a base with a LITERAL-ZERO index (the `p = PT(0)` loop-head class the superseded record correctly excluded), nothing about non-pointer scalar locals, and nothing about references with no constant offset to place. The mutual-exclusion clause is measured on a short-circuit `&&` chain; it is not claimed for a conditional expressed as a separate statement-level branch with the pointer live across it.

falsifier: Exhibit an MWCC 1.2.5 function in which a pointer local holding base + scaled_index is ASSIGNED under a conditional branch and the compiler still emits the constant in the load DISPLACEMENT (a `lwz disp(rX)` after an `add`), rather than folding it into the index with an indexed load. That single case would show the conditional assignment does not forfeit the displacement form and that the coupling asserted here is site-specific rather than general. Conversely, to disprove the declaration-site refutation specifically, produce two builds differing ONLY in whether such a pointer is declared at the enclosing block top or inside the conditional block, whose objects are NOT byte-identical; that is the exact comparison run here (probes B and C) and it must be re-run from a clean HEAD with `probe.py --discard` between the two, because a BEST anchor banked by an earlier probe makes both read as regressions against each other rather than as equals.
subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: FOR A POINTER LOCAL HOLDING base + scaled_index, IT IS THE ASSIGNMENT SITE AND NOT THE DECLARATION SITE THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE TRAILING CONSTANT LANDS IN THE LOAD DISPLACEMENT OR IN THE INDEX -- AND THE DISPLACEMENT FORM AND A LATE base+index ADD ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. Measured on do_players' two twin j-loops, whose target shape is `add r4,r31,r3` ; `lwz r0,3368(r4)` against our baseline `addi r0,r3,3368` ; `lwzx r0,r31,r0`. Three forms, each applied identically to both twins, each measured from HEAD: (A) `u8* jrec = (u8*)potionicon_tab + j * PREC_STRIDE;` as an UNCONDITIONAL block-top initialiser flips the addressing form exactly as claim.law.direct-global-member-flips-index-base-association predicts -- both `lwzx` vanish, the opcode multiset goes 14t -> 12t -- but MWCC then schedules the base+index `add` ABOVE the short-circuit branch it belongs under, converting each cluster from an addressing-form difference into a one-slot schedule difference (real 840 -> 852, fresh fuzzy 97.2692 -> 96.8433). (B) declaring AND assigning the same pointer inside `if (j != i)` reverts the addressing form COMPLETELY -- 14t, both `lwzx` restored, cluster rows textually identical to baseline -- at real 864 and frame 264 -> 272. (C) declaring at the block top but ASSIGNING inside the same `if` produces output BYTE-IDENTICAL TO B: real 864, multiset 14t, frame 272, same 21-cluster list. THE B/C PAIR IS THE PROOF, because those two differ ONLY in declaration placement and produced literally the same object; the A/C pair differs only in assignment placement and produced different objects. This REFUTES the declaration-site clause of claim.law.PC_a-named-pointer-local-selects-the-displacement-load-and-its-declaration-site-decides-the-hoist.20260902.v1 at the first site where that law was ever IN scope -- the superseded run-38 record had correctly refused to apply it at a `p = PT(0)` loop head for want of a scaled index, so the clause had never actually been tested against one. The law's first half survives: a named pointer local DOES select the displacement load. Its second half is wrong about which site controls it. CONSEQUENCE FOR MATCHING: when the target shows a displacement load whose base+index add sits AFTER a short-circuit branch, pointer-local spelling cannot reach it. The unconditional assignment buys the displacement and forces the early add; the conditional assignment sinks the computation and forfeits the displacement. Stop after the second form and record the coupling rather than spending a third -- and note that a third form differing only in declaration placement is NOT a distinct axis, because it cannot move the deciding variable.
